supporting_observations.claim: The supplied records show recurring HTTPS CONNECT attempts to update.chartmate-imaging.net at 13:38:00, 13:43:20, 13:47:44, 13:52:37, 13:58:16, 14:03:02 and 14:08:00 UTC, consistent with the alert's roughly five-minute cadence.

Endpoint and connection records attribute these proxy connections to PID 3416, C:\Users\ben.carter\AppData\Local\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe, running as ben.carter. The process was launched by explorer.exe at 13:37:57 and terminated at 14:08:34 UTC.

The executable path and destination differ from the supplied approved ChartMate configuration: the observed executable is under the user's AppData rather than C:\Program Files\ChartMate, and the destination ends in .net rather than the approved .com. These discrepancies make a benign updater disposition unsupported without validation, but do not alone prove impersonation or malware.

Five CONNECT attempts established tunnels, each reporting 5,397 client-to-server bytes and 31,383 server-to-client bytes. Two other attempts returned proxy authentication-required and gateway-error responses; those attempts are not evidence of successful HTTPS exchanges with the destination.

A Sysmon file-creation event attributes creation or overwrite of the AppData cmupdate.exe path to PID 3416 shortly after its first recorded tunnel. This merits examination but does not establish a malicious self-update.

known_telemetry_limitations: The successful CONNECT records expose tunnel metadata, not decrypted requests, responses or transferred content (T015-00110, T015-00209, T015-00264, T015-00269, T015-00281).
The supplied process and file records do not provide executable hashes, signature validation or file contents for cmupdate.exe (T015-00108, T015-00114).
The provided collection-status metadata reports a WS-LPARK-01 endpoint-log outage from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC; it does not report an outage on the alerted workstation.
claims_not_established: Whether the AppData executable is authentic ChartMate software or an impersonating binary (T015-00108).
Whether update.chartmate-imaging.net is a legitimate vendor endpoint or attacker-controlled infrastructure (T015-00110).

Whether the recurring tunnels carried update traffic, command-and-control messages or sensitive data; timing and byte counts alone do not establish their purpose (T015-00110, T015-00209, T015-00264, T015-00269, T015-00281).
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire the AppData cmupdate.exe, compute its hash, validate its signature and compare it with a trusted vendor package; examine installation provenance and the file event at 13:38:01 UTC (T015-00108, T015-00114).
Confirm with the software owner or vendor whether the AppData installation path and .net endpoint are legitimate supported configurations (T015-00108, T015-00110).

Obtain destination DNS/TLS details and any available decrypted proxy or endpoint HTTP telemetry for the recorded tunnels to determine their actual content and purpose (T015-00110, T015-00209, T015-00264, T015-00269, T015-00281).
unrelated_findings: Separately review an anonymous NTLM network logon to FILE-HD-01 from WS-BCARTER-01 at 13:54:48 UTC. The supplied records do not link it to PID 3416 or the recurring HTTPS activity, so it does not decide this alert (T015-00253, T015-00257).
